_doc: c3's declaration of how the Containers page groups containers by PROJECT and by KIND (owner request 2026-11-04). Owner rule: a container belongs to the app or project it IS, not to whose data it holds. A container's project is, in order: (1) its explicit `name_overrides` entry (container name -> project id), (2) the first project whose `folder_prefix` (its cloudy-u-containers folder, containers-declared.json `dir`) or `name_prefix` matches, (3) `default` (the explicit Others bucket, no silent fallback to Cloudy). Prefixes serve containers not yet listed in name_overrides. `code` is the project's code in the fleet registry. The page strip is declared in build.json (ui.sections[containers]; since #1941 one page per project, grouped on the first row by the project's `category`); a project listed there with no match here shows an empty page, honestly. `kinds` are the page-wide Filters (All | MCPs | APIs | Apps | DBs | Repos), drawn once above the project tabs: a container takes the first kind whose name rule (name_suffix / name_contains) matches, else the first whose category_prefix matches, else `default_kind`. `kinds[].role` matches the entity role, and an entity takes EVERY kind that names its role: a git repo (a data store: both Repos and DBs, so it shows under both filters; its db_engine is git) (data/repos_declared.json, generated from the fleet registry by data/gen_repos_slice.py) is the Repos kind. A project with `repo_group` (Cloudy) keeps the containers' own macro groups and lists its repos in that group; every other project's groups are its registry FAMILIES (CG, Capital, Hardtech, Cloud-me, Others): a repo sits in its family, a container in `container_family` (container name -> family) else in `container_group`. `group_remap` moves every container of a macro group to another group of the document (Project Apps -> Cloud Apps: projects are the tabs now, so no tab shows a Project Apps group; the Infra Apps and Cloud Apps macro groups are Cloudy's only), in both Topology and Table.
proj_doc: #1941 the Project of a container is one of the Cloud Me > Proj entries (ac_cloud-me/build.json ui.sections[proj]: category = the Proj group, label = category_name, spelled as that data spells it) plus Lib for libraries (registry 6.3 Library-KG) and the All view; `category` is the first row of the Containers page, a project's own label is its second row. A JVM test holds this list against the Cloud Me data. A project with no `code` has no repo in the registry.
type_doc: Type (App | Db | MCP | API | Repo | Other) is derived from the kind of a container: a git repo is Repo, else the kind's `type_of_kind` entry, and an App in one of `other_categories` (net, mesh, builders, gits, infra, backup: the plumbing) is Other.

topology_layout._doc: #1953 the Topology body of every project page (and All) is two bands: services (Apps, DB, MCP, API, Other) and Repos. Every Type of `types` sits in exactly one section (a test pins the union). `split` declares a Public / Private part split per project and section, by visibility (a repo's `visibility`, a container's isPublic). A section with nothing in it draws no card; a band with nothing in it prints one line, never vanishes. Each part shows the old `<group> · <category>` sub-headers.

lfs._doc: #1953 E a repo the registry flags `lfs: true` is a git-lfs DATABASE: its Type is type_of_kind[type_kind] (Db) and its db engine `db_engine`; it is drawn under DB only, not also under Repos.

project_repos_doc: #1953 C repos the registry code cannot place on a project (its code is blank or holds no registry repo): data/gen_repos_slice.py attaches them (via "declared") with an optional path inside the repo. Same answer as Cloud Me's proj-repo-urls-1932.json (a drift test compares both).

aliases._doc: #1968 Lib is renamed Wiki: its old project/category ids resolve to the Wiki project that now holds its repos (lib-chronos primary on Wiki_ModernSc, the hubs over it and the root _git-repos-master on Wiki_Projects). ui.aliases.pages in build.json carries the same ids for the app routes.

projects_table._doc: #1969 Infra > Projects: the columns, the filter chips (column keys) and the page a row tap opens ({project} = the project id: its Containers Topology). One row per project above; nothing here is typed in Kotlin.

vm_view.host_order_doc: #1971 the order of the VM pages after All, as declared (never sorted in code); a derived host not listed here follows in the fleet's order, the unknown host is always last.
vm_view._doc: #1971 Containers has two top modes: Projects (the category strip, as before) and VM (the containers by the host they are deployed on). The VM pages (build.json containers pages with this id prefix) are one per DERIVED host: every fleet VM that holds a declared container (fleet_slice.json vms, alias = the container's host) plus every mesh-client device (fleet_slice.json electronics with a wg_ip), then `unknown` for a container whose host is none of them (each such host value is named with its reason). `all` is every container plus the repos; a repo has no host, so it shows in All only, under the repos band relabelled here, with its reason line. Page ids are `<page_prefix><host id>`.
vm_view.repos_reason: Repos are git repositories: they are deployed on no host, so they are listed here, in All only.
vm_view.unknown_reason: host {host} is not a declared fleet host (no VM or mesh-client device has it), so its containers are kept here, never dropped.
